newsitem.title: FRANCE: Barry Callebaut plans stock listing in early 1998.
newsitem.headline: Barry Callebaut plans stock listing in early 1998.

text.p: Barry Callebaut, the company formed by the merger of France's Cacao Barry SA and Swiss Callebaut AG, plans to seek a stock market listing in early 1998, a Callebaut official said.

"The company could be listed on the stockmarket during the first six months of next year, initially in Zurich and then probably in Paris and in Brussels," the vice chairman of Barry Callebaut's board, Charles Gebhard, told a press conference. a "We are currently merging the activities of the two companies in various countries. The initial public offering could take place early next year," he said.
Gebhard said the company planned to increase its capital and that would take place at the same time as the market listing.
"The initial idea is to increase our capital by 25 to 30 percent, depending on market conditions," he said.
Gebhard said the Klaus J. Jacobs holding company, which currently controls 100 percent of Barry Callebaut, would remain a majority shareholder upon completion of these operations.

The February merger of Cacao Barry and Callebaut AG created a company with sales of 1.7 billion Swiss francs, operating profit of 111.7 million Swiss francs, after-tax profit of 59.7 million and cashflow of 112.7 million.

Data for the first half of fiscal year 1996-97, the six months to February 28, showed sales of 1.04 billion Swiss francs, operating profit of 81.8 million Swiss francs, after-tax profit of 44.4 million and cashflow of 80.1 million.
